subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core plugin-runtime circuit breaker now, and what API, storage model, operator controls, and default fail modes should it expose?
rationale: This would create new plugin runtime semantics, persisted state, operator surfaces, and compatibility-sensitive default behavior that automation cannot safely choose from source inspection alone.

options.title: Approve staged core breaker design
options.body: Define SQLite-backed breaker state, passive telemetry, status/reset commands, and plugin-declared degradation contracts before enabling automatic quarantine.

options.title: Keep breakers plugin-owned for now
options.body: Leave framework behavior unchanged and ask high-risk plugins to implement local circuit breakers through existing hook/config surfaces.

options.title: Start with passive telemetry only
options.body: Add hook timing and error counters without quarantining plugins, then decide active open/half-open behavior after deployment evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve staged core breaker design
recommendation.body: Define SQLite-backed breaker state, passive telemetry, status/reset commands, and plugin-declared degradation contracts before enabling automatic quarantine.

likelyOwner.reason: The current plugin hook runner and registry history make vincentkoc the best available owner for the core runtime/API decision.
